newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - June 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - June 18.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Three men disguised as preachers abduct a Filipino-Chinese realtor in southern Iligan city. (MANILA STANDARD)

- Eight Moslem guerrillas and a soldier are killed in a clash when Army troopers move in to free 43 oil comapny workers held captive by the rebel group in southern Maguindanao province. (PHILIPPINE STAR)
- Chief presidential legal adviser Rene Cayetano says efforts to push the amendment of the Charter through a people's initiative are doomed. (MANILA CHRONICLE)
- The Philippine Army placed on alert its unit in the countryside following a series of attacks by communist rebels in Bicol and Western Visayas. (PHILIPPINE DAILY INQUIRER)
- International investment house Salomon Brothers wins the bidding to underwrite the Central Bank's yankee bond flotation. (ALL PAPERS)

- Securities and Exchange Commission officials deny the existence of a report that allegedly found foreign stockbrokers conspiring to manipulate prices at the Philippine Stock Exchange. (BUSINESSWORLD)
- The country's year-on-year trade deficit narrowed by 34.8 percent to $860 million in the first four months of the year from $1.319 billon, the National Statistics Office says. (BUSINESS DAILY)
